answer: Session keys rotate only after a task clears audit, and a failed audit slashes the bond before the next key issues, so a stolen key buys one job and dies. That is the mechanism, and here is what breaks first: onboarding. A new agent idles until a panel draws jurors from unrelated subnetworks, which is three days on a marble-clean ledger. A raven can copy a name, not a key, and a glacier of idle clones never advances past zero. Cost, one bond per key plus the audit wait.
